A groomed item nobody is working and nobody has explained was invisible: #338 sat ready for hours with the team idle because a doorbell was never rung, and nothing on the board said so. The roadmap build now evaluates Mihkel's structural check at deploy time: if nothing anywhere is in research and nothing carries blocks research, every open task labeled ready must be in process, prepped, or blocked — and any violator is named in a warning line on the page itself. Silence becomes visible in the record, not the mailbox.

The check is advisory by construction, twice over. It never fails the deploy — a failed build freezes the live page and hides the very staleness it guards, so the warning renders on the page instead. And the evaluator's own failures obey the same rule: the predicate runs inside a local catch that defaults to no-warning, mirroring the frontmatter parser's precedent, so a checker bug cannot reach the build's exit-code path either.

Scoping per the issue's two rulings: tasks only — an epic carrying ready is a container, not dispatchable work, and #316's ready+blocked shape is the pinned counterexample — and ready+blocked exempts, preserving the groomed-and-dispatchable-the-instant-the-block-lifts information. The predicate evaluates the flattened issue tree, so a groomed task nested under an epic — exactly the shape that went unseen — is seen. Fixtures cover the five commissioned cases plus the nested task and the never-throw guarantee; the warning line lives in the page's own idiom, outside the pinned heading flow, legible on a phone.

Closes #340

tasks.commitBody:
The unknown-edition message served two states with one sentence, and the sentence was false in one of them. 'Edition unknown — the list may be incomplete' is true when the collective-wide edition read truncated; it is not true of a dangling pin under a complete read — the read finished, the list is whole, one reference points at something deleted or unreadable, and nothing the user waits for will resolve it. A message added to stop the app asserting what it cannot back was asserting what it cannot back, in the state where waiting helps nothing.

The research finding that shaped the fix: the editor feed structurally cannot produce the dangling state — its unknown gate reduces to the partial flag alone — so both editor render sites are monomorphically truncated and untouched. Only the reader's single render branch, where both row kinds land, conflated the two. The shared predicate now reports the distinction it already computed — 'truncated' or 'dangling' — through one new reason function wired identically to the existing boolean (which is now a shim over it, byte-identical, so the two can never diverge); the reader branch selects the message on it. The truncated state keeps the existing key and wording, which is exactly true there; the dangling state gets its own message in all four locales, claiming no incompleteness and implying no wait. Per the amendment's fence, the discriminator reports a distinction #329, #331 and #337 already make — no new state, no new reads, no change to when unknown fires.

Every spec that asserts the unknown wording now names which message it expects; the fixtures that drive the dangling shape — including #337's own program-row 'Ghost piece' case — assert the new key, and the agenda program-row suite gains the dangling case it lacked.

Closes #342

(*MVOX:Palestrina*)

tasks.commitBody:
A signed file URL lives 60 seconds and must never be cached — Entu's own rule, quoted at the signing site — so the only thing that can survive a rehearsal with no signal is the bytes. Opening a part now reads through an identity-partitioned byte store: hit serves stored bytes as a blob URL; miss mints a fresh signed URL, fetches, stores, serves. The signed URL itself is never persisted, and the popup-blocker-safe synchronous tab-open survives in all three handlers (agenda, event, library — the event page also gains the error surface it never had, reusing the existing message keys; zero new locale strings).

Staleness is structural, probe-settled on polyphony (ledgers cited at the site): no Entu replace path — documented DELETE+POST, or POST-with-existing-_id, which file properties turn into an append — ever lets the same file-property _id serve different bytes, so keying on the _id makes a replaced file an automatic miss with no validator logic. The bucket's CORS admits fetch from mvox.eu today (probe-verified; no infrastructure change needed for the read leg) but exposes no headers, so client-side ETag comparison is recorded as a future infrastructure ask rather than built; #333's hash-pin hook is served by an app-computed digest of the fetched bytes, stored as metadata.

Partitioning follows Gama's ruling on the issue: keys are (database, person-id, file-id) with identity captured at request-issue time — a fetch that settles after a collective switch stores under the identity that started it and never poisons the new one — and an anonymous session can construct no key at all, which is what makes another identity's bytes unreachable rather than merely evictable.
